lines.text: What if humans never learned to control fire?
A million years ago, our ancestors gathered around their first campfires. Now imagine that spark never caught.

segments.caption: Chewing all day
segments.fact: RAW FOOD FOR A HUMAN BRAIN

lines.text: Without cooking, everything is eaten raw: roots, leaves and tough meat.
To feed a brain like ours on raw food, we'd need to eat for more than nine hours a day.
Many scientists think cooking freed up the energy to grow our big brains.
Without it, our ancestors might have kept smaller brains, bigger jaws and bigger bellies.
Nights are pitch black and cold, with no fire to keep predators away.
And nobody sits around the flames telling stories.

segments.caption: Stuck in the warmth
segments.fact: NO FIRE TO SURVIVE THE COLD

lines.text: Without fire for warmth, the icy north would be far harder to settle.
Humans might never have spread across the whole planet.

segments.caption: No metal
segments.fact: NO POTTERY · NO GLASS · NO BRICKS

lines.text: No fire also means no pottery, no glass and no bricks.
And metal? Copper only melts at over a thousand degrees, so the Bronze Age never begins.
No steam engines, no power plants, no factories, no rockets.
Even today, most of the world's electricity comes from burning fuel.
Today, there might be no cities at all. Just small groups of humans, foraging under the sun.
So, was fire our most important discovery?
